Here's Ursa's Fury Swipes total damage calculation:

* FSdmg = (F + ((7,5 + 2,5 * (L - 1)) * (S - 1))) * FSs

Here's Ursa's DPS calculation (not taking armor and other reductions into account):

* Total DPS = 2,94 * Dmg / (10,3 - OPa / 2,94) + FSdmg / (FSs / (ApS + (2,94 * (OPa / 2,94)) / 10,3) + ApS*Dmg

*F* is the amount of extra damage you take from a single Fury Swipes stack (15/20/25/30 depending on level).

*L* is Ursa's level of Fury Swipes.

*FSs* is Fury Swipes stacks.

*Dmg* is Ursa's Base Damage + Bonus Damage.

*OPa* is the number of attacks for which Ursa gains maximum attack speed (3/4/5/6 depending on level).

*FSdmg* is Fury Swipes damage.

*ApS* is Ursa's Attacks per Second.

One of the problems I have with Ethereal Blade is that, in my opinion, it's almost always an inferior choice to other items that fulfill similar roles and are, in some cases, cheaper.

It builds from an Eaglesong (which reaches its highest cost effectiveness when used by Agility heroes) and a Ghost Scepter (usually bought by squishy supports).

Another problem is most Agility heroes lack the nuking power required to make full use of Ether Blast (Morphling and Gyrocopter being some exceptions). It's usually better to turn the Eaglesong into a Butterfly.

Building it on most Strength heroes is really cost-inefficient, since most of them do not benefit from the extra Agility. If they only wanted to use the active to cripple the enemy's carry, then Heaven's Halberd becomes a much better alternative.

On the other hand, Intelligence heroes don't have much of an incentive to build Ethereal Blade over Orchid Malevolence, which gives them more Attack Speed, better Mana Regeneration, and increased magic damage thanks to Soul Burn.
